title: Pull-Up Resistors
summary: How do engineers prevent floating pins?

steps.title: Pull-Up Resistors
steps.markdownContent:
### Anchoring the Voltage: The Pull-Up Solution
How do engineers prevent floating pins? We anchor the pin to a known voltage using a **pull-up resistor**!

A pull-up resistor connects the input pin to **+5V**. When the switch is open, the resistor gently "pulls" the pin up to 5V, guaranteeing a stable, rock-solid `HIGH`.

```
Button OPEN (Idle):
  +5V ---[ 10k Resistor ]---> Pin 2 (Reads HIGH, 5.0V)
                                |
                           [ Switch: OPEN ]
                                |
                               GND
```

### Why a Resistor Instead of a Plain Wire?
Why not connect Pin 2 directly to +5V with a solid wire? Consider what happens when someone presses the button to GND:
- If you used a plain wire from 5V to the pin, pressing the button would connect **+5V directly to GND with ZERO resistance**!
- This creates a **dead short circuit**, drawing massive current, heating the wires, and triggering USB shutdown protection!

### Ohm's Law to the Rescue:
With a 10,000Ω (10kΩ) pull-up resistor in place:
$$I = \frac{V}{R} = \frac{5.0\text{V}}{10{,}000\Omega} = 0.0005\text{ A} = 0.5\text{ mA}$$
When the button is pressed, only half a milliamp of current flows safely to GND, pulling Pin 2 all the way to **0.0V (LOW)** with zero danger!

### Active-Low Logic:
Notice the logic pattern in this circuit:
- **Button Released (Idle)**: Pin 2 reads **`HIGH`** (+5V).
- **Button Pressed (Active)**: Pin 2 reads **`LOW`** (0V).
Because the active state is `LOW`, this is called **active-low logic**!

quickCheck.question: What hazardous condition occurs if you connect +5V directly to Ground with a plain wire and no resistance?
options: A dead short circuit that draws extreme current and can damage hardware
The microcontroller automatically increases its clock speed
The breadboard changes color to blue
quickCheck.explanation: Joining power and ground with negligible resistance causes a dead short circuit, risking silicon damage.
quickCheck.warmupExplanation: Current equals voltage divided by resistance (I = V/R). Zero resistance leads to dangerous overcurrent.

quickCheck.question: In an active-low circuit with a pull-up resistor, what voltage level does the pin read when the button is pressed to GND?
quickCheck.explanation: Pressing the button connects the input directly to GND, pulling the pin voltage down to 0V (LOW).
quickCheck.warmupExplanation: Active-low circuits connect the input to ground when pressed, registering as LOW (0V).

steps.title: Tying Inputs to +5V Safely
steps.markdownContent:
Pull-Up Circuit Architecture
A 10k resistor connects the pin to +5V. When the button is unpressed, the pin reads HIGH. When pressed to GND, it reads LOW.

questions.question: What state does a pull-up resistor keep a pin in when the button is NOT pressed?
questions.explanation: The pull-up resistor pulls the pin voltage up to +5V (HIGH) until grounded!

questions.question: Why is a 10k resistor used instead of a direct wire to +5V?
options: To limit current when the button connects the pin directly to Ground
questions.explanation: Without resistance, pressing a button connected to GND would cause a direct short circuit!
